summary: Teardown (thiscall) of a track-object manager: frees every heap array stored in the object at offsets 0x0..0x68 (dword slots 0..26). Simple pointer arrays are freed directly via FreeWrapper_7bcf (allocation bases are stored 4 bytes before each array, hence the -4 adjustment); large struct arrays (792/808-byte elements at 0x2C, 0x38, 0x44, 0x50) run per-element destructors first (ShortComputation_fd70 via explicit reverse loop or ArrayDestructorIterator); 36-byte element arrays (0x40, 0x4C, 0x58) are walked with ArrayDestructorIterator using the no-op EmptyStub_aa60; trailing arrays (0x5C, 0x64, 0x68) are released through ArrayOfObjectsDestructor / ShortComputation_fda0. All freed slots are zeroed in batches. Delegated from DelegationThunk (0x0040E1C0).

operations.description: Guard on this+0x8 non-null: the combined pointer array (slot 2) is passed directly to FreeWrapper_7bcf with no base adjustment.
Zero the first batch of fields: this+0x0 (total count), this+0x4 (capacity), this+0x8 (combined array pointer).
Free the vehicle data array: snapshot this+0x10 (slot 4), then FreeWrapper_7bcf(this+0x10 - 4) using the stored allocation base.
Zero this+0xC and this+0x10 (vehicle count and vehicle data array pointer).
Free the dspoly/dsindicator small array: snapshot this+0x18 (slot 6), then FreeWrapper_7bcf(this+0x18 - 4).
Zero this+0x14 and this+0x18 (dspoly count and small array pointer).
Free the non-DSP node array: snapshot this+0x20 (slot 8), then FreeWrapper_7bcf(this+0x20 - 4).
Zero this+0x1C and this+0x20 (non-DSP count and small array pointer).
Free the cone small array: snapshot this+0x28 (slot 10), then FreeWrapper_7bcf(this+0x28 - 4).
Zero this+0x24 and this+0x28 (cone count and small array pointer).

Teardown the 792-byte element array at this+0x2C (slot 11): read element count from *(array - 4), walk the elements in reverse calling ShortComputation_fd70 per element, then FreeWrapper_7bcf(array - 4).
Free the post small array: snapshot this+0x34 (slot 13), then FreeWrapper_7bcf(this+0x34 - 4).
Zero this+0x24, this+0x28 and this+0x2C (cone count, cone small array pointer, cone large array pointer).
Teardown the 792-byte element array at this+0x38 (slot 14): read count from *(array - 4), walk elements in reverse calling ShortComputation_fd70, then FreeWrapper_7bcf(array - 4).
Zero this+0x30, this+0x34 and this+0x38 (post count, post small array pointer, post large array pointer).
Teardown the 36-byte element array at this+0x40 (slot 16): ArrayDestructorIterator(array, 36, count, EmptyStub_aa60) walks elements with the no-op stub destructor, then FreeWrapper_7bcf(array - 4).
Teardown the 792-byte element array at this+0x44 (slot 17): ArrayDestructorIterator(array, 792, count, ShortComputation_fd70), then FreeWrapper_7bcf(array - 4).
Zero this+0x3C, this+0x40 and this+0x44 (sign count, sign small array pointer, sign large array pointer).
Teardown the 36-byte element array at this+0x4C (slot 19): ArrayDestructorIterator(array, 36, count, EmptyStub_aa60), then FreeWrapper_7bcf(array - 4).
Teardown the 808-byte element array at this+0x50 (slot 20): ArrayDestructorIterator(array, 808, count, ShortComputation_fd70), then FreeWrapper_7bcf(array - 4).
Zero this+0x48, this+0x4C and this+0x50 (wheel count, wheel small array pointer, wheel large array pointer).
Teardown the 36-byte element array at this+0x58 (slot 22): ArrayDestructorIterator(array, 36, count, EmptyStub_aa60), then FreeWrapper_7bcf(array - 4).
Zero this+0x54, this+0x58 and this+0x5C (wing count, wing small array pointer, wing large array pointer).
Guard on this+0x5C non-null: release the wing large array through ArrayOfObjectsDestructor(3); the constant argument 3 is the value present in the raw source.
Guard on this+0x64 non-null: release the part small array through ShortComputation_fda0(3); the constant argument 3 is the value present in the raw source.
Zero this+0x54, this+0x58 and this+0x5C (wing count, wing small array pointer, wing large array pointer) after the wing large array release.
Guard on this+0x68 non-null: release the part large array through ArrayOfObjectsDestructor(3).
Zero the final batch: this+0x60, this+0x64 and this+0x68 (part count, part small array pointer, part large array pointer).
ShortComputation_fd70 (0x0040FD70) is used as the per-element destructor for the large 792/808-byte struct arrays (also referenced as a global here).
Delegated from DelegationThunk (0x0040E1C0), which drives the whole teardown.

clean_pseudocode: for (char *p = arr + 792 * n - 792; n--; p -= 792) ShortComputation_fd70(p);
unresolved: The callees ArrayOfObjectsDestructor(0x0040FDD0) and ShortComputation_fda0(0x0040FDA0) are invoked with the constant argument 3 while the guarded object slots (0x5C, 0x64, 0x68) are not passed to them; the decompiled raw source shows the constant, so the true argument was likely folded away by the compiler.

Object class identity: existing analysis names it the track object manager and pairs each slot with a semantic purpose (vehicle/dspoly/non-DSP/cone/post/sign/wheel/wing/part), but no static owner is confirmed.
Field 0x8 (slot 2) is freed directly without the -4 base adjustment applied to every other array slot.
